narrative.overview:
Numbered Evidence is a compact personal workbench, not a decorative report editor. Navy frames the workspace, ice blue separates work areas from near-white records, and cobalt makes references and selected paths visible. Dense rows, stable IDs, fixed readiness cells, and one aligned evidence trace make the path from captured work to reviewed reporting inspectable.

This document records the shared visual world of the shipped Numbered Evidence production UI: the shared shell plus the Timeline, Plans, Reports, and report workspace surfaces, with the remaining Library and configuration pages inheriting that shell. They implement the user-directed C hybrid composition: B’s 248px period sidebar combined with C’s split body, persistent context, and report-first review. The approved hybrid is now the production system; A and B survive only as historical prototype alternates, and the development-only `/prototype` switcher is not part of production.
keyCharacteristics: Stable `@id`, `%id`, and `Rid` references remain visible beside content.
Explicit labels and values accompany green, amber, neutral, and error states.
Compact controls, tabular numerals, thin dividers, and small radii prioritize scanning.
Navy is structural; cobalt marks action, selection, citations, and trace alignment.
Source draft, candidate final, and human adoption remain visibly distinct.

rules.name: The Citation Rule
rules.body: Cobalt identifies an actionable or traceable path; do not use it as general decoration.

rules.name: The Monochrome-Proof Rule
rules.body: Status color always travels with an explicit word, number, icon, or shape so meaning survives without hue.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Geist Sans serves both controls and report content; do not introduce a display serif or separate monospace for citations.

rules.name: The Stable-Number Rule
rules.body: IDs, dates, counts, revisions, and period ranges use tabular numerals wherever alignment matters.

rules.name: The Flat Record Rule
rules.body: Evidence rows, readiness cells, source panes, and report documents use boundaries and tonal contrast, not ambient card shadows.

rules.name: The Shared Selection Rule
rules.body: Selected text uses navy ink on the cobalt highlight tint (`#bcd3fa`) with a cobalt caret in every workbench surface; never leave a report, preview, plan, or proposal module on the browser default selection.

dos: Do keep `@id`, `%id`, and `Rid` adjacent to the records they identify and align numeric operational data.
Do preserve the four readiness cells and the single Live event → Next snapshot → Review trace when reorganizing a surface.
Do keep Leadership and Personal scopes, snapshots, source drafts, finals, and review states explicitly separate.
Do pair every status color with visible language or a check/shape, and retain the shared focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use compact white records on ice work areas, with navy reserved for shell, capture, and decision gates.
donts: Don't turn evidence rows into floating cards or use cobalt as a decorative accent detached from action, selection, or traceability.
Don't collapse source draft, candidate final, and human adoption into one visually undifferentiated document state.
Don't treat a source draft as a final, enable adoption without final content, or imply that live edits rewrite a frozen report basis.

Don't replace the shipped C hybrid with the A or B prototype compositions; they are historical alternates only, and the `/prototype` variant switcher and its throwaway components are development tooling, not production code.
